title: Quasi-finite boundary of fibrewise nonempty opens in good curve compactifications
statement: Let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $I$ be a finite set and, for every $i\in I$, let $t_i:T_i\to B$ be finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], let $b_i:C_i\to T_i$ be smooth and proper [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-proper-morphism], and suppose every fibre $(C_i)_s$ is nonempty, geometrically connected and of dimension at most one [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $u_i:O_i\hookrightarrow C_i$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $(O_i)_s$ is nonempty for every $s\in T_i$. Put $C=\coprod_{i\in I}C_i$ and $O=\coprod_{i\in I}O_i$, regarded as an open subscheme of $C$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and let $Z=(C\setminus O)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow C$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Then the induced morphism $Z\to B$ is separated, quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Empty $I$, empty $B$ and empty $T_i$ are permitted.

proof.text: For each $i$, the finite morphism $t_i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Therefore $f_i=t_i\circ b_i:C_i\to B$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. In particular each $f_i$ is separated, of finite type and universally closed, by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

The clopen components of $C=\coprod_i C_i$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] let us check properness directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For an affine open $V\subset B$, each $f_i^{-1}(V)$ has a finite affine cover by finite-type $\mathcal O_B(V)$-algebras; their union over the finite set $I$ gives the same kind of cover of $f^{-1}(V)$, so $f:C\to B$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The target $C\times_B C$ of its diagonal is covered by the open pieces $C_i\times_B C_j$: pulling back the two open component decompositions gives this cover. On a piece with $i\ne j$ the inverse image of the diagonal is empty; on a piece with $i=j$ it is the closed immersion $\Delta_{f_i}$. Thus its inverse image on every affine chart of such a piece is a quotient by an ideal, so $\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion by the affine-local criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Finally, after any $B'\to B$, the pullbacks of the clopen components are again disjoint and cover. A closed subset restricts to a closed subset in each component; its image in $B'$ is the finite union of their closed images, hence closed. Thus $f$ is universally closed and therefore proper. All three checks also hold for $I=\varnothing$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], $Z\to C$ is a closed immersion with underlying image $C\setminus O$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] to the proper morphism $C\to B$ from step 2: $h:Z\to B$ is proper. Hence $h$ is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $B$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] gives local finite presentation of $h$. It is quasi-compact because it is of finite type. Its diagonal is a closed immersion by separatedness, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and therefore of finite type and quasi-compact. Thus $h$ is also quasi-separated, and the finite-presentation convention in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] shows that $h$ is of finite presentation.

Fix $i\in I$ and $s\in T_i$, and put $X=(C_i)_s$. Properness survives this base change by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], so $X$ is separated and of finite type over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole ring), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. The fibre-smoothness clause of [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] makes $X$ smooth over $\kappa(s)$. Since $X$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(s)$ and smooth, the forward implication of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-smooth-field-criterion], applied with the finitely generated (by no elements) extension $L=\kappa(s)$, for which $X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\cong X$ by its first projection, shows that every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a regular local ring; as $X$ is Noetherian, $X$ is regular. This criterion holds over any field, with no perfectness, dimension or algebraic-closedness hypothesis. Geometric connectedness includes connectedness over the identity field extension [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; $X$ is nonempty by hypothesis. The final assertion of [rem-pc-regular-normal] therefore gives that $X$ is irreducible. This argument uses neither a perfect residue field nor dimension exactly one.

Let $U=(O_i)_s\subset X$. The homeomorphisms from scheme fibres to the topological point-inverse-images in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], together with the open-subscheme identification [def-weil-open-immersion], identify $U$ with an open subset of $X$; it is nonempty by hypothesis. Schemes are Kolmogorov: if two points had the same closure, that irreducible closed subset would have two generic points, contradicting [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Thus [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed] applies to the irreducible space $X$ of dimension at most one and to $U$. It makes every point of the closed subset $E_{i,s}=X\setminus U$ closed in $X$. Since $X$ is Noetherian, [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] gives that $E_{i,s}$ is finite. In dimension zero the conclusion is stronger: $U=X$, because any point of its complement would give a proper nonempty irreducible closed subset of the irreducible zero-dimensional space $X$.

proof.text: Fix $b\in B$. For each $i$, the finite morphism $t_i$ is quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf], so [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] says that $S_{i,b}=t_i^{-1}(\{b\})$ is a finite set. The component description [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and the image statement [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identify the underlying set $h^{-1}(\{b\})$ with the disjoint union, over $i\in I$ and $s\in S_{i,b}$, of the sets $E_{i,s}$ of step 5: a point of $Z$ lies in a unique $C_i$, its image under $b_i$ is a unique $s$, and it is outside $O_i$. Here [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies points of $(C_i)_s$ with points of $C_i$ mapping to $s$; no base-change invariance of the reduced subscheme structure is asserted or needed. There are finitely many indices and each $E_{i,s}$ is finite. Hence $h$ has finite fibres.

We proved in step 3 that $h$ is of finite type, hence locally of finite type and quasi-compact, and in step 6 that all its fibres are finite. Apply the reverse implication of [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres]: $h$ is quasi-finite. Its separatedness and finite presentation were already established in step 3. If $B$, $I$, or a particular $T_i$ is empty, the corresponding point or component arguments are vacuous; an empty component contributes no points and all conclusions remain valid.
